title: Care Pathway Analysis of Children and Adolescents with Chronic Pain – Barriers and Facilitators to Access Specialized Pediatric Pain Centers (SPPC)
summary:
Chronic pain in childhood and adolescence severely impairs the quality of life of those affected, leads to high socio-economic costs and increases the risk for chronic pain conditions in adulthood. According to the current knowledge, treatment in specialized pediatric pain centers (SPPC), providing interdisciplinary assessment and interdisciplinary, multimodal pain therapy, is to be pursued for optimal care of young patients. However, there is evidence that patients obtain access to such suitable care facilities only via long detours. To date, research on the details of care pathways of children and adolescents with chronic pain is very limited. This results in a lack of approaches on how access to SPPCs can be improved.
Thus, the objective of this study is to characterize the care pathways of children and adolescents with chronic pain and to investigate which barriers and facilitators exist to the access to SPPCs in the German healthcare system. Therefore, an anonymous online survey is conducted to collect quantitative data. Children and adolescents suffering from chronic pain, their guardians (usually the parents) as well as general practitioners, specialist physicians and psychotherapists, who treat children and adolescents with chronic pain in private practice, at outpatient facilities or at an SPPC, are surveyed. At participating SPPCs, the young pain patients and their parents are asked retrospectively about their journey through the healthcare landscape from symptom onset to their first presentation at the SPPC. Surveys on barriers and facilitators are conducted among children and adolescents with chronic pain, their guardians and the addressed healthcare providers.
Characteristic pathway sequences of children and adolescents with chronic pain in the German healthcare system are identified by means of care pathway analyses (patient journey mapping). Furthermore, it will be investigated whether and to what extent the different care pathways are associated with patient characteristics (sociodemographic and pain-specific variables) as well as with perceived barriers and facilitators.
Results of this study can inform decision-makers in the German healthcare system about the current status of care pathways of children and adolescents with chronic pain and the associated barriers and facilitators to the access to SPPCs. These insights can guide new approaches for improving the care structure for this vulnerable patient group.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Children and adolescents with chronic pain and their guardians:
•	admission to the SPPC no more than three months ago 
•	statutory or private health insurance in Germany 
•	German language proficiency
•	intellectual ability to answer a questionnaire
•	written consent to anonymous data usage
Healthcare provider:
•	completed training as a medical specialist or psychological psychotherapist
•	treatment of children and adolescents with chronic pain for at least one year
•	provision of services within the German healthcare system
•	written consent to anonymous data usage
Exclusion criteria:
Children and adolescents with chronic pain and their guardians:
•	malignant disease of the child/adolescent
•	severe mental disability of the child/adolescent
•	severe congenital physical disability of the child/adolescent
•	life-limiting illness of the child/adolescent
•	minor age of the legal guardian
Healthcare provider: none
